title: POC scoping — NovaHealth quality eval plan
summary: AE+SE call to finalize POC success criteria and agree a quality evaluation plan: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, scoring. Discussed workload sizing, benchmark targets, timelines and next steps for pilot. Security/PHI considerations flagged; Redwood to share SOC2 + onboarding checklist.
topics: Quality evaluation plan: golden prompts, scoring rubric, regression suite

Maya Rodriguez: export 500 sample prompts + 100 golden responses (anonymized) - 2026-12-08
Sofia Chen: prepare benchmark config and cost estimate for 1 week run - 2026-12-06

transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - Alex from Redwood, Sofia our solutions engineer, Jared from success.
[00:07] Dr. Patel: Hi Leela here, and Maya and Owen and Samir on. Sorry late.
[00:12] Alex: no worries. We're here to lock down the POC success criteria and the quality evaluation plan, especially golden prompts and hallucination checks.
[00:23] Sofia (SE): Quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, golden prompts/regression tests, scoring rubric, timeline. We'll go deep on scoring because we want the pass/fail to be deterministic for the POC.
[00:34] Samir (Product): that's key for us; our clinical triage flow can't slip on hallucinations, so we need clear thresholds.
[00:40] Maya: agreed. Also want to be realistic on throughput. Our peak is about 80 QPS for the triage API (burst to 120). Baseline latency target is 250ms p50 and 600ms p95 for short prompts.
[00:51] Sofia: ok, sizing note - for the POC we'll run sample traffic at 20, 50, and 80 QPS to see degradation. We'll recommend Dedicated for steady 80 QPS, hosted for lower.
[01:05] Dr. Patel: on quality - we want golden prompts: can you outline what you mean?
[01:10] Alex: golden prompts are a curated set of representative user inputs with a human-vetted expected output. For the POC we recommend 100-200 golden prompts spanning positive cases, edge cases, and failure modes.
[01:24] Alex: the golden set will include examples for: correct clinical extraction, recommended next steps, and safe-fallback phrasing when model unsure.
[01:33] Maya: we can anonymize and share 500 sample prompts; narrow 100 as golden. We'll need guidance on formatting.
[01:40] Sofia: format guidance: provide prompt text, expected structured output (JSON schema), and acceptability tolerances (e.g., exact match for codes, soft match for free-text explanation). We'll share a template.
[01:52] Dr. Patel: what about hallucination checks?
[01:55] Sofia: we propose two tiers: 1) Entity hallucination: model invents patient data or test results - auto-fail. 2) Clinical recommendation hallucination: unsafe or unsupported recommendations - fail threshold at >1% of golden prompts. We'll run automatic checks with heuristics + human review sample.
[02:12] Alex: plus format checks: enforce JSON schema compliance on structured outputs. If output fails schema, it's a functional fail.
[02:20] Samir: OK, scoring - what's the rubric?
[02:24] Sofia: scoring mix: 50% functional correctness (schema + entities), 30% clinical accuracy (human review on a sample), 20% safety/hallucination metrics and latency/throughput SLOs. We'll compute a composite score; threshold for POC success 85/100.
[02:38] Dr. Patel: can that be broken down into pass/fail gating? We want hard gates for hallucination and schema compliance.
[02:44] Sofia: yes - gating rules: schema compliance must be >= 98% on golden prompts; entity hallucination rate must be < 1%; clinical accuracy (sampled human labels) must be >= 90%. Composite score then confirms overall health.
[02:57] Maya: what about regression tests? We have previous model outputs from last vendor; we want to ensure new model doesn't regress on intent/labels.
[03:05] Alex: we'll import their historical test-suite. Regression tests: run their baselines and current Redwood model, compute delta on key metrics (F1 on entity extraction, exact match on codes). Regression threshold: no more than 2% drop on core metrics.
[03:20] Owen (Security): PHI concerns - will sample data be shared? We need to know encryption in transit/storage and retention.
[03:27] Jared (CSM): quick note - Redwood supports encrypted transfer, we can sign an NDA, and for POC we recommend de-identified data unless your security team signs the DPA. We'll share SOC2 + data flow diagram.
[03:40] Owen: please send the DPA and SOC2. Also need to confirm that private deploy is an option if we can't share PHI.
[03:47] Alex: yes, Private (VPC/on-prem) is an option; for the POC we can do hosted with synthetic/anonymized data and then switch to Private if needed.
[03:55] Samir: benchmarks - what baselines do you plan to run?
[03:59] Sofia: baseline models: open LLM v1 (their current vendor), Redwood-curated 7B quantized, and a 13B variant. We'll run quality eval (golden prompts) plus throughput tests at 20/50/80 QPS. We'll capture latency p50/p95, token cost, and the scoring metrics.
[04:17] Alex: cost estimate for a 1-week benchmark run: we'll provide a rough number in the template. For the POC acceptance, we want cost per inference and error rate to meet thresholds.
[04:27] Dr. Patel: timeline - when can we kick off?
[04:30] Alex: proposed timeline: this week - share template + security docs; next week - NovaHealth shares samples; wk of 12/13 - benchmark runs; 12/20 - results + joint review; 12/22 - sign POC acceptance or iterate.
[04:44] Maya: that timeline works but we need to align stakeholders. We'll need Samir + clinical SME available for human labeling on sample subset (about 100).
[04:53] Samir: can do.
[04:56] Dr. Patel: what's the human labeling workflow?
[04:59] Sofia: short: we'll provide a web labeling sheet with instructions and example judgments. We ask NovaHealth to label ~100 golden outputs for clinical accuracy. We'll also do automated heuristics across full set.
[05:12] Alex: one more thing - regression guardrails: we'll snapshot baseline outputs and track diffs. If regression occurs beyond 2% we'll pause rollout and require remediation.
[05:22] Owen: audit logging - retention window? We need 12 months for audit purposes.
[05:27] Jared: Redwood can enable extended retention as an add-on; we'll include options in the security packet.
[05:34] Maya: example golden prompt types - triage question, symptom extraction, medication extraction, suggested next step (non-prescriptive).
[05:42] Alex: sample golden prompt example: prompt text: "Patient reports chest pain and shortness of breath, age 62, history of HTN." Expected output (schema): {symptoms: [...], severity_score: 0-3, suggested_next: [Escalate to ED | Schedule urgent appointment | Self-care], confidence: 0.0-1.0}. Exact match required for coded fields, fuzzy allowed for suggested text.
[06:05] Samir: for confidence thresholds - we want model to output confidence and for low confidence fallback to human triage.
[06:12] Sofia: we'll include confidence-based routing as part of the POC: if confidence < 0.6, route to human. We'll measure how often that would have triggered.
[06:20] Dr. Patel: what about format errors - incomplete JSON etc?
[06:23] Sofia: those are auto-fails on schema compliance. We'll also run a post-processor to attempt safe reparsing (e.g., add closing braces) but count original failure for the metric.
[06:33] Maya: what should we expect in the eval deliverable?
[06:36] Alex: final eval deliverable: a report with composite score, per-metric breakdown (schema compliance, hallucination rate, clinical accuracy), latency/cost numbers, regression diffs and recommended next steps. We'll include raw logs and labeling sheet.
[06:50] Dr. Patel: can we have a pass/fail example?
[06:53] Sofia: pass if: composite score >= 85, schema compliance >= 98%, hallucination < 1%, clinical accuracy >= 90%, regression drop <=2%, and latency/p95 within agreed SLO.
[07:05] Maya: sounds good. Please send templates.
[07:08] Alex: will do - alex@redwood.com, i'll drop the spreadsheet and the benchmark config.
[07:13] Jared: i'll attach SOC2 and the onboarding checklist.
[07:16] Owen: we'll review DPA with legal and get back.
[07:19] Dr. Patel: thanks - last question on tooling: do you provide evaluation scripts?
[07:24] Sofia: yes, we'll provide the repo with scripts to run the scoring, but note: some clinical judgments require human review, so scripts will compute auto metrics and produce artifacts for labeling.
[07:36] Alex: ok wrapping - recap of next steps and owners. Thanks everyone.
[07:42] Dr. Patel: thanks all.
